# Background and aim

## Stress responses & perseverative cognitions

\fontsize{9pt}{10}\selectfont
__Perseverative cognitions__ (PC) = “repeated or chronic activation of the cognitive representation of one or more psychological stressors” \fontsize{6pt}{10}\selectfont \newline (Brosschot et al., 2006) \fontsize{8pt}{10}\selectfont

- Re-enactment of past stressors (**rumination**) \newline and anticipation of future stressors (**worry**)

- PC trigger and prolong stressor-related physiological activation, \newline possibly leading to long-term health consequences

- Main pathogenic mechanism of psychological stress?

```{r , echo = FALSE, out.width="190px",fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("img/pc.png")
```

## Sleep quality and primary insomnia: \newline The hyperarousal hypothesis

## Sleep-related **H**eart **R**ate **V**ariability

\fontsize{9pt}{10}\selectfont
__(Resting-state) HRV__ = Beat-to-beat fluctuations in inter-beat intervals in phase with respiratory cycles \fontsize{8pt}{10}\selectfont

- Index of cardiovascular health & vagal
cardiac control \fontsize{6pt}{10}\selectfont (Shaffer et al, 2014; EU Society of Cardiology, 1996) \fontsize{8pt}{10}\selectfont

- Primary allostatic load mediator, primary output of Central Autonomic Network, predictive of individual differences in emotion regulation, sensitive to stress and workplace stress \fontsize{6pt}{10}\selectfont (Jarczok et al, 2013) \fontsize{8pt}{10}\selectfont

- Increasing trend throughout the night

```{r , echo = FALSE, out.width="240px",fig.align='center'}
knitr::include_graphics("img/night_hrv.png")
```

## Technology-Assisted Supplemental Work (TASW)

\fontsize{8pt}{12}\selectfont
= Performance of “role-prescribed tasks at home \newline after regular work hours with the aid of technological tools” \newline \fontsize{6pt}{8}\selectfont (Fenner & Renn, 2010)

# Method

## DARE project

## The sample so far

```{r , echo = FALSE, out.width="70px"}
# reading data
rm(list=ls())
load("data/DATASETS/ema_clean.RData") # long-form
pq <- read.csv("data/DATASETS/t1_clean_ema.csv")

# pairing codes
pq$ID[pq$ID=="e13b797"] <- "e13n797"
pq$ID[pq$ID=="l04a701"] <- "m04a701"
pq$ID[pq$ID=="v29n267"] <- "v29n2672"
p <- levels(as.factor(tolower(ema$ID)))
p_prel <- levels(as.factor(tolower(pq$ID)))
# p[!p%in%p_prel] # only EMA: "j74db" "r14b722" "s10s644"
# p_prel[!p_prel%in%p] # only pq: "glnav" "s10t644" "sara7"  

# removing participants included in one but not in the other
ema$ID <- tolower(ema$ID)
pq$ID <- tolower(pq$ID)
ema <- ema[ema$ID %in% p[p%in%p_prel],]
pq <- pq[pq$ID %in% p_prel[p_prel%in%p],]

# recoding remote work
pq$remote <- FALSE
pq$remote[pq$job.hours_remote>0] <- TRUE

# response rate
for(i in 1:nrow(pq)){
  pq$rrate[i] <- nrow(ema[ema$ID==pq$ID[i] & ema$aft==1,]) +
    nrow(ema[ema$ID==pq$ID[i] & ema$eve==1,]) +
    nrow(ema[ema$ID==pq$ID[i] & ema$mor==1,]) }
```

\fontsize{10pt}{12}\selectfont

`r fontawesome::fa(name = "user", height = "1em")` `r fontawesome::fa(name = "user", height = "1em")` `r fontawesome::fa(name = "user", height = "1em")`  \newline
`r nrow(pq)` employed adults \fontsize{8pt}{12}\selectfont (`r round(100*nrow(pq[pq$gender=="F",])/nrow(pq),1)`%F, `r round(mean(pq$age),1)` $\pm$ `r round(sd(pq$age),1)` y) \newline
Job tenure: `r round(mean(pq$job.tenure),1)` $\pm$ `r round(sd(pq$job.tenure),1)` y, `r round(mean(pq$job.hours),1)` $\pm$ `r round(sd(pq$job.hours),1)` hrs/week \newline
`r (round(100*table(pq$job.position)/nrow(pq)))[1]`% employees, `r (round(100*table(pq$job.position)/nrow(pq)))[4]`% managers, `r 100 - ((round(100*table(pq$job.position)/nrow(pq)))[1]+ (round(100*table(pq$job.position)/nrow(pq)))[4])`% other \newline 
`r (round(100*table(pq$remote)/nrow(pq)))[2]`% remote/hybrid workers 

\fontsize{10pt}{12}\selectfont
__Recruitment__ \fontsize{7pt}{12}\selectfont \newline
Convenience sampling, 5-day EMA &rightarrow; €10-25 reward + individual report \newline \fontsize{9pt}{12}\selectfont  `r sum(pq$rrate)` observations, `r nrow(ema)` workdays \newline
Response rate = `r round(100*mean(pq$rrate/15),1)`% $\pm$ `r round(sd(100*pq$rrate/15),1)`% 

\fontsize{10pt}{12}\selectfont
__Exclusion criteria:__ \fontsize{8pt}{10}\selectfont

- Unemployed/Students/Trainees

- < 6 work hours/day

- Nocturnal shifts

- Careless resp. (attention checks)

- Manual workers

- Full remote workers

```{r , echo = FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
library(multilevelTools)
tasw <- 
  round(omegaSEM(items=paste0("tasw",1:4), id ="ID", 
                 data=ema)$Results[1:2,2],2)
pc <- 
  round(omegaSEM(items=c(paste0("pcb",1:3),paste0("pcf",1:3)), id ="ID", 
                 data=ema)$Results[1:2,2],2)
sq <- 
  round(omegaSEM(items=paste0("sd",1:4), id ="ID", 
                 data=ema)$Results[1:2,2],2)
```

# How should I analyze it?

## Alternative statistical methods \newline for modleling 3-level time series

- Night-specific slope as `Y` variable

- 3-level LMER

- Growth curve model

- Dynamic SEM

## Night-specific slope as `Y` variable: \newline Back to 2-level comfort zone

```{r , echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
# step 1
for(id in unique(ema$ID)){
  for(night in 1:4){
    ema[ema$ID==id & ema$day==night,"HRV_slope"] <-
      summary(
        lm(RMSSD ~ time + RMSSD_lag, data = sleepHRV)
      )$coefficients[2,1]
  }}

# step 2
m <- lmer(HRV_slope ~ pc + tasw + (1|ID), data = ema)
```

## 3-level LMER \newline Will it ever converge?

```{r , echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
m <- lmer(RMSSD ~ time + time:pc + time:tasw + 
            RMSSD_lag + (1|ID:day), 
          data = sleepHRV)
```

## Growth curve model with MPLUS

```{r , echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
VARIABLE: NAMES ARE ...;
          USEVAR ARE ...;
          WITHIN = time;
 !#and what about day-level variables? 

ANALYSIS: TYPE = THREELEVEL RANDOM;
          ESTIMATOR = MLR;

MODEL: %WITHIN%
       slope | RMSSD ON time;

       %BETWEEN%
       slope ON tasw;
       slope ON pc;
```

Not sure about how doing this with `lavaan`...

## Idiographic latent profile analysis (???)

```{r , echo = FALSE, out.width="250px"}
knitr::include_graphics("img/lpa.png")
```

\fontsize{7pt}{12}\selectfont
"*The present study used idiographic (i.e., N = 1) LPA to extract and group together similar measurement occasions from an individual’s time series data. Broadly, LPA uses continuous (or ordinal; Van Lissa et al., 2024) indicators to identify subgroups in the data. In our case, LPA probabilistically classifies each measurement occasion into a subgroup, separately for each person. The subgrouping procedure results in a set of similar moments that can be summarized as a personality facet profile (15 total variables in each profile) unique to the individual.6 A measurement occasion is grouped with another if both have sufficiently similar indicator values and covariances. Idiographic LPAs were estimated using the Mclust package (Scrucca et al., 2016, 2023) in R (R Core Team, 2024).*"
